title: AI-powered attacks on Korean financial sectors linked to Chinese DDoS group: report
key_facts: Seoul-based security firm Logpresso said in a report released Sunday that the Telegram account 'YY520CN', linked to the bank hackings, was listed in September 2024 as a moderator of the online community GodNet.
GodNet was created by Vitas, a Chinese group that carries out distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks, which flood a service with traffic, for paying clients.
Logpresso's findings come from analysing a report released earlier this month by US firm CrowdStrike, which compared Telegram and GitHub records with data stolen by infostealer malware.
Logpresso traced a second GodNet staff account, linked to GitHub code and an email address whose logins were stolen by infostealer malware in 2023, including Microsoft and Oracle cloud logins.
Logpresso says the account links alone do not establish who carried out the hacks and it could not conclude only one person was behind the breaches.

The YY520CN account was deleted on 8 Oct; a new account with the same name later posted a denial of involvement, and the owner of the linked phone number also denied involvement, saying their number was used without permission.

South Korean authorities suspect the attacker combined AI models, including DeepSeek, with ARTEX to hit seven South Korean financial institutions in succession; ARTEX's developer has halted updates and public distribution.
quote_evidence: The company said the Telegram account "YY520CN," linked to the bank hackings, was listed as a moderator of an online community called GodNet in September 2024.
But the company said the account links alone do not establish who carried out the hacks, and it could not conclude that only one person was behind the breaches.
The account was deleted on Oct. 8, after the report was released.
why_it_matters_hint: A possible lead to the people behind the attacks on South Korean banks, though Logpresso itself says it proves nothing about who did it.
event_date: Logpresso report released Sunday 11 Oct 2026; CrowdStrike report 7 Oct 2026
notes: Korea Herald text says Logpresso's report was released Sunday; the article is dated 11 Oct 2026. It cites Reuters for the ARTEX developer's decision.
